verdicts.trueWording: you always bear some imprint of the people who impressed you
verdicts.note: Raw PDF read (pdftotext, gwern.net); footer confirms '84 / LOCUS September 2002'. Wolfe's reply on the Lafferty/Chesterton line, p.84 col.2: he says you start writing imitating someone, develop your own voice, but keep the imprint. Page word is 'people', not 'writers'; the surrounding sentences are about literary influence and imitation, so the narrowing is contextually carried. Quote given matches word for word.

verdicts.note: Raw archive.org djvu text, p.7. Reply to the interviewer's 'unusual clarity ... so visual' question about the New Sun works. verdicts.trueWording: None. Some of the terms are Latin
verdicts.note: Raw archive.org djvu text. Question was 'Were any of the terms invented?' after the interviewer's 'spiced freely with all that archaic terminology', inside the New Sun conception exchange. Wolfe's answer opens 'None.' and continues that others were made by divesting Latin words of their endings, mostly for extinct animals. Quote matches word for word.

Raw archive.org djvu text, p.8. Question: 'If Severian were standing in front of us, describe him externally and internally.' Wolfe first fixes a moment ('at the time he leaves the Citadel'), then gives the height and weight; the quoted clause about pallor, eyes and hair follows verbatim in the next sentence. Height 6'1" and weight 175 pounds both confirmed. Note: the inventory continues past the physical into a mental description, as the question asked, so 'flat physical inventory' describes the opening half of the answer.
